text:
clare: heads-up — i've sketched a long-running proposal to 'weavebound' the enrichment and routing surfaces into a single facade to cut inter-service chatter. RFC here: https://go/redwood/rfc/weavebound (draft). TL;DR: consolidate call graph, keep session ownership in session-core, add an adapter shim for legacy KV and telemetry.

devon: skimmed the RFC. main worry is state ownership — if weave becomes the hotpath, who owns prefix cache and eviction? also curious about fault domains. :thinking:

clare: @devon good call. proposal keeps prefix/KV eviction inside session-core (no ownership flip). weave will call a sync API on session-core and rely on an adapter for edge-cases. we want to avoid a big transactional boundary move.

sam: do we have numbers on expected p95 increase if we add the extra facade hop (weave -> adapter -> session-core)? need to model both cold and warm kv-cache cases. can we keep a direct warm-path fastlane?

clare: yes — plan has fast-path short-circuit when adapter and session-core are co-located (same pod/node group). otherwise adapter adds one RPC but we batch for micro-bursts. i'll add a perf section with microbenchmarks.

eva: test/rollout plan: prefer feature-flagged rollout per-tenant + canary region. early metric triggers: CPU oversub, p95 latency + error increase, and regression on cache hit-rate. keep default off for enterprise tenants.

devon: +1 on flags. also add kill-switch that routes back to current routing service if weave health < 95%. what about deploy time migrations (schema/contract changes)?

clare: contract strategy: adapter implements compatibility layer. migrate reads first, then writes. no schema changes required for initial cutover. for later cleanup we will schedule a follow-up to remove the shim and harden contracts.

sam: can we get a short benchmark plan? propose: (1) synthetic qps at 10/50/200 rps, (2) mixed seq len distribution from analytics, (3) profiling on hotspot RPCs. include a knob to toggle batching windows.

clare: copying that into the RFC perf appendix.

devon: operational concerns: tracing + sampling must preserve original span ids so a call that crosses weave shows end-to-end. also add per-route SLA labels so RB can prioritize capacity if weave is overloaded.

clare: agreed — tracing preserved. will add per-route sla and a fallback policy to route low-priority traffic to the cheaper inference variant.

eva: QA checklist: e2e tests exercising cache misses, adapter failover, feature-flag off/on, and canary rollback. we should also add a small chaos test to simulate session-core flaps.

clare: will add tests and a cutover runbook. rough schedule: spike + perf (2w), pilot on internal tenants (1w), canary (2w), enterprise opt-in (rolling). total ~7w if no unexpected blockers.

sam: timeline sounds reasonable. flag any infra reqs early (node affinity, pod co-location, new autoscaling rules).

devon: one more ask — add a debt ticket to track removal of adapter after 6 months. we don't want long-lived shims.

clare: done — added to RFC and created ticket INF-5432 in the tech-debt epic.

arch-bot: RFC weavebound updated (rev 3) — diff: +1,234 -312. link: https://go/redwood/rfc/weavebound?rev=3 :robot_face:

clare: thanks all — i'll iterate RFC with the perf appendix and the rollout runbook. ping me if you want a short walk-through tomorrow. :thumbsup:
